source_text: Tempus admonet ut ad alia transeamus; sed quoniam certum est, nihil te habere quod vendites imperitis auribus praeter verecundiam naturalium; quam brevissime potero, quod putatur superesse, contingam. Quis ergo neget, honestatem hanc, qua genitalia nostra contegimus, pro personis, locis, officiis moribusque variari? Sic in conventiculis publicis obscenior nuditas, nihil habet turpitudinis in lavacris. Sic alter est cubicularis habitus, seminudus et securus; alter vero forensis, sollicitior et profusior. Quid, quod ad testimonium crebro familiaritatis, respicit negligentia cautionis, et quanto persona aut ignotior aut honoratior adfuerit, tanto diligentior habitus comparatur? Quid, quod nautis et opificibus plerisque nemo vitio nuditatem dedit? Ac ne ista simplicitas personis magis quam negotiis imputetur, more omnium etiam Petrus apostolus, et post resurrectionem Domini nudus in navigio piscabatur [n76] . Dirige hinc oculos ad medicantum munera; ducunt artem studio salutis in locos pudoris. Athletis nuditas etiam decora est. Iam vero non solum adolescentulis, et petulanti sibi societate coniunctis, sed etiam totis quibusdam gentibus uterque sexus retectus, et sine secreti est electione commixtio. Quid tamen mirum, si id Scotus vicinarumque gentium barbaries agat; cum et philosophia, cuius supra commemorationem fecimus idem censuerit, et Traducianorum huc dogma pervenerit? Quae ergo pudoris tenebitur quantitas, quive limes inter tot eius diversitates, atque inter coeptus partim necessarios, partim societate defensos, per quem possit doceri, diabolum naturalem ardorem sexibus miscuisse? Ac per hoc, ut praesidium opinionis tuae constat, officiis, locis, moribus, artibus et totis simul gentibus dissolutum; ita remansit invictum, quod nos ipsa ratione et apostolo Paulo docente defendimus, omnia corpora, omnia membra corporum, omnesque sensus corporum, Deum auctorem universorum creasse; sed ita ordinasse, ut quaedam in membris nostris pro opportunitatibus temporum amiciret pudor, quaedam honestas naturalis offerret, quibus tam indecorum esset tegimen adhiberi, quam importune genitalium vulgare secretum.
pass_a_gloss: Time warns that we pass to other things; but since it is certain that you have nothing to sell to unskilled ears besides the reverence of natural things, as briefly as I shall be able I will touch what is thought remaining. Who therefore would deny that this honorableness by which we cover our genitals varies according to persons, places, offices, and manners? Thus in public assemblies a more obscene nakedness has nothing of turpitude in baths. Thus one is the bedroom habit, half-naked and secure; but another the forensic, more anxious and more ample. What of this, that the negligence of caution looks to the testimony of frequent familiarity, and the more unknown or more honored the person present, the more diligent a habit is furnished? What of this, that to sailors and to most craftsmen no one gave nakedness as a vice? And lest that simplicity be imputed more to persons than to businesses, by the custom of all even Peter the apostle, and after the Lord's resurrection, was fishing naked in the boat. Direct eyes from here to the offices of physicians; they lead the art by the zeal of health into places of modesty. For athletes nakedness is even becoming. Now indeed not only for youths and those joined to themselves in a wanton society, but even for certain whole nations both sexes are uncovered, and mingling is without choice of secrecy. Yet what wonder if a Scot and the barbarism of neighboring nations do this; when even philosophy, of which we made commemoration above, judged the same, and the dogma of the Traducians has arrived here? What quantity of modesty therefore will be held, or what limit among so many diversities of it, and among beginnings partly necessary, partly defended by society, through which it can be taught that the devil mixed a natural ardor into the sexes? And through this, as the protection of your opinion stands dissolved by offices, places, manners, arts, and whole nations together; so that has remained unconquered which we defend by reason itself and with the apostle Paul teaching, that God the author of all things created all bodies, all members of bodies, and all senses of bodies; but so ordained that modesty would clothe certain things in our members according to the opportunities of times, and natural honorableness would offer certain things, to which it would be as unseemly for a covering to be applied as it is untimely to make public the secret of the genitals.

pass_b_english: The time urges us to move on to other matters. But since you plainly have nothing to peddle to uneducated ears except modesty about natural functions, I will touch as briefly as possible on what seems to remain. Who denies that the decency with which we cover our genitals varies according to persons, places, occupations, and customs? Thus nakedness that would be quite obscene in public gatherings carries no shame in the baths. The dress of the bedroom is one thing, half-naked and carefree; dress in public is another, more careful and more ample. Again, neglect of precautions often indicates familiarity: the more unknown or honored the person present, the more carefully one dresses. And no one has blamed sailors or many craftsmen for nakedness. To show that such simplicity belongs more to the work than to the person, even the apostle Peter, following everyone’s custom, fished naked in the boat after the Lord’s resurrection (John 21:7). Turn your eyes next to the work of physicians: in their care for health they apply their art to the parts modesty conceals. Nakedness is even becoming to athletes.

Moreover, not only among young people bound together in a wanton companionship, but even among certain whole nations, both sexes go uncovered and unite without choosing a private place. Yet why be surprised if a Scot and the barbarity of neighboring peoples do this, when the philosophy mentioned above judged the same thing acceptable, and the doctrine of the advocates of inherited sin has arrived at the same point? What fixed measure of modesty, what boundary, can be maintained amid so many variations, and amid practices defended partly by necessity and partly by companionship, by which it could be proved that the devil mixed natural ardor into the sexes? Your opinion’s support has plainly been dissolved by occupations, places, customs, arts, and whole nations together. Meanwhile, what I defend through reason itself and the teaching of the apostle Paul remains unconquered: God, the author of all things, created every body, every bodily member, and every bodily sense. But he arranged them so that, as occasions require, modesty should clothe some of our members and natural decency should display others. It would be as indecent to cover these others as to expose the privacy of the genitals at an unsuitable time (compare 1 Corinthians 12:23–25) (1 Corinthians 12:23–25).

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
